title: fix(approvals): serve the approval request definitions to the callers the approvals door admits
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DJEiaSe88RGo8NywXBBGbvk)_

Fixes #32955

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: none — `schemaReadDelegate` is a plugin-owned delegate key like `fileAccessDelegate`, which no published skill teaches; it names a kernel service, and only plugin code can provide one

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：审批申请和审批动作这两个对象（`sys_approval_request`、`sys_approval_action`）的定义，重新对「审批门认可的人」开放：在本组织里至少能看到一张审批单的人，即当前审批人、提交人、已经处理过的人，以及有越权审批权的管理员。开放方式是由审批插件在这两个对象上声明 `schemaReadDelegate: 'approvals'`（新增的对象键，仿照已有的 `fileAccessDelegate`），元数据接口在对象读权限拒绝之后才去问审批服务；网关里没有对象名单。
- 为什么改：#32428 之后，普通成员读不了的对象在元数据接口上一律当作不存在。这两个对象按设计只能经 `/api/v1/approvals/*` 读行，所以非管理员审批人打开审批单时拿到 404，页面显示「Object Not Found」，没有审批按钮。这是 18.4.0 的发布阻断项。
- 风险与回滚：只放开「定义」，不放开「行」：数据门对审批人照旧拒绝；字段级安全照样裁剪下发的定义；与本组织任何审批单无关的成员照旧 404，对象列表里也看不到这两个对象（别的组织里的审批记录不算数）；其它所有对象的答案不变（钉子测试逐项比对了列表）。REST、调度器和两种 MCP 出口答案一致。审批服务出错时答 5xx，不会误答「不存在」。回滚即 revert 本 PR，退回到 404 的现状。
- 先看：`packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts`（`admittedBySchemaReadDelegate`：只在读检查拒绝后、字段姿态已确定时才问）、`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`（`authorizeSchemaRead`：复用审批单读门自己的可见规则）、`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`（`resolveObjectMasker` 接线）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run --project isolated test/approval-request-schema-party-read.dogfood.test.ts`，预期 1 passed（审批人和提交人 200、陌生成员 404、数据门仍拒绝）。
- 需要你做的：本 PR 改了 ADR-0106（受治理面，Tier H），需要你本人合并，或由 GOVERNED_APPROVERS 之一批准后由席位落地。
- 请你确认一处措辞：ADR 新加了一条约束，以后任何别的对象再声明这个键，都算对裁决 6787890900 的又一个例外，必须先记入 ADR-0106 并按同样规则审查后才能上线。若你觉得太严，可以放宽为「按上述规则审查即可」。

## What changes

- **`@objectstack/spec`:** a new optional object key, `schemaReadDelegate`, beside `fileAccessDelegate`. It names a kernel service that implements `authorizeSchemaRead(objectName, context)`. Its reference docs, authorable surface and liveness entry are regenerated.
- **`@objectstack/metadata-core`:** `resolveObjectSchemaMaskPosture` takes an optional `schemaReadDelegates` source. When `canReadObject` refused the caller and the caller's field posture is determined, it asks the object's declared delegate; only `true` turns `hidden` into the caller's own field posture. A declared delegate that is missing or has no method leaves the object absent (warned once); one that throws is `ObjectSchemaMaskEvaluationError`, the D6 tier-3 fault. `objectSchemaReadDelegateSource` builds the source from a transport's engine and service lookups.
- **Transports:** `RestServer.resolveObjectMasker` (via a by-name service lookup that `RestApiPlugin` passes as a new last constructor argument), the dispatcher's `resolveObjectMasker` in `domains/meta.ts` (which the HTTP MCP object tools share), and the stdio MCP bridge (`callerObjectView` / `createStdioDataBridge`, wired by `MCPServerPlugin`) all hand the posture the same source, so every schema-serving outlet gives one answer.
- **`@objectstack/plugin-approvals`:** `sys_approval_request` and `sys_approval_action` declare `schemaReadDelegate: 'approvals'`. `ApprovalService.authorizeSchemaRead` refuses every other name, and for these two answers whether the door serves the caller at least one request in their organization: `visibleRequestIds` (the rule `getRequest` and `listActions` apply), then one `sys_approval_request` read scoped like `findRequestRow`, because the already-acted probe is not organization-scoped. The verdict is kept per request context, so an object list asks once.
- **ADR-0106:** an "Exception (2026-11-13)" section records maintainer decision 6840464379 as an exception to ruling record 6787890900, with its anchor invariant. `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` says who is served the two definitions.

## Why

Since #32428, the metadata API answers an object the caller may not read as absent (ruling record 6787890900). `sys_approval_request` and `sys_approval_action` are closed to ordinary members on the data side on purpose, and their rows reach a member only through `/api/v1/approvals/*`. So a non-admin pending approver got `404` on both definitions, and the console request page rendered "Object Not Found" with no decision actions. The maintainer decided (6840464379) not to revert #32428: these two definitions become visible to the callers the approvals door admits, declared by the owning plugin rather than a name list in the gate, with rows still only through the approvals door and field security still applied.

## Acceptance notes

- **Rows reach no new caller.** The data door still asks `canReadObject` and the ObjectQL middleware; the diff touches neither. The HTTP pin asserts `/data/sys_approval_request`, `/data/sys_approval_request/:id` and `/data/sys_approval_action` still refuse the approver.
- **No other object's `hidden` answer changes.** The delegate is asked only after the read check refused, and only for an object that declares one; `authorizeSchemaRead` refuses any name but its two. The pin asserts the approver's object list is exactly the stranger's list plus the two declared objects, and the closed sibling `sys_approval_approver` stays `404`.
- **Field security still masks the served schema.** An admitted caller is served their own field posture. The pin withholds `node_config_json` from the approver and asserts it is absent from what they are served (and present for the submitter). An undetermined field posture never asks the delegate, because admitting there would serve the schema unmasked.
- **A member party to no request learns nothing new.** The stranger gets `404` on both and neither is listed. A unit test pins the cross-organization case the red-line re-read found: a decision taken in another organization does not admit a member who is party to nothing in their own. That case is fixed in this PR.
- **List semantics.** The list asks the same posture per object, so an object is listed to exactly the callers its item read serves.
- **The predicate is the door's own rule.** It admits past actors and commenters, and the override holder, as the door does. The opt-in record-reader tier (#8652) is evaluated only against a named record, so a viewer admitted only by that tier still gets `404` on the definitions. That fails closed; it is the one place the predicate is narrower than the door.
- **An emptied projection stays a fault.** If field security leaves an admitted caller no field of either object, the outlet answers 5xx as it does for a reader of the object (D6, #3545). Not changed here.
- **Cost.** One verdict per request. The already-acted probe scans `sys_approval_action` by `actor_id` / `acted_as`, which carry no index; the inbox already runs the same probe on every list. An index is a follow-up, not part of this fix.
- **Contract.** Clause-② widening (an object that answered absent is now served to some callers) and a new authorable key; `RestServer` gains an optional last constructor argument.
- **Governance.** The ADR path makes this Tier H: a maintainer merge, or approval from a governed approver before the seat lands it. The key itself can be written on any object, so nothing mechanical holds the exception to these two. The ADR closes that gap in text: any further declaration is a further exception to ruling record 6787890900, recorded in ADR-0106 and reviewed against the same rules before it ships.

## Tests

- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-request-schema-party-read.dogfood.test.ts` (HTTP, real stack): admin control `200`; pending approver and submitter `200` on both, listed, approver's served fields lack the withheld field; stranger `404` on both and on `sys_approval_approver`, not listed; approver's list = stranger's list + the two; approver's data reads refused. **Red on main** `25ee5076` (`approver sys_approval_action … expected 404 to be 200`), green here.
- **Ablation:** with `schemaReadDelegate: 'approvals'` removed from `sys-approval-request.object.ts` (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restored to HEAD), the pin goes red: `approver sys_approval_request … expected 404 to be 200`.
- `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.test.ts`: admitted and projected; only `true` admits; not asked when readable, exempt or masking is off; undeclared or no source stays hidden; undetermined stays hidden unasked; missing service warns once; a throw is the fault; the source reads the live registry and resolves the engine once.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts`: approver and submitter admitted, stranger refused; answers by `visibleRequestIds`; counts only requests in the caller's organization (shown to bite by removing the organization filter); asked once per request context; refuses other names; both objects declare the delegate.
- `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.object-schema-mask.test.ts`: the stdio tools serve an admitted principal the projected object and keep it absent for a refused one; `MCPServerPlugin` wires the source for both tools and resources.
- `packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin-slot-lookups.test.ts`: the new last `RestServer` argument is classified in the provider span, and its own case pins that it looks a service up by name on the kernel of the environment asked for, answering `undefined` for a name nothing registers.

## Verification

All at head `ff77f21ea0`. `origin/main` was merged twice:
- once before this PR opened (`ae9c13407e`);
- once more for a conflict, at `870ce55ab2`. That conflict was in the spec generated files only; they were regenerated from the merged tree and committed.

- **Derived gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` gave 133 commands. Each ran with its exit code recorded before any pipe, and all 133 exited 0. `pnpm lint` exited 0. `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran ran.list`: *133 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 133 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED* (exit 0).
- **Governed surface:** `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --test <three-dot file list>` exits 3 (`GOVERNED`, landing tier **H**). The trigger is `docs/adr/**` ×1, `docs/adr/0106-metadata-plane-fls-object-schema-masking.md`.
- **HTTP pin:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run --project isolated test/approval-request-schema-party-read.dogfood.test.ts` gives 1 passed on the merged tree. It is red on main `25ee5076`, and red under the ablation above.
- **Unit suites on the merged tree** (every one exits 0):

  | Package | Test files | Tests |
  |---|---|---|
  | `@objectstack/metadata-core` | 27/27 | 1024/1024 |
  | `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` | 118/118 | 1623/1623 |
  | `@objectstack/mcp` | 63/63 | 1095/1095 |
  | `@objectstack/rest` | 408/408 | 8309 passed, 332 skipped |
  | `@objectstack/runtime` | 591/591 | 10449 passed, 19 skipped |

  The rest run caught one thing: the new last `RestServer` argument had not been classified in `rest-api-plugin-slot-lookups.test.ts`. It is now classified there and has its own case.
- **Typecheck:** `typecheck` exits 0 on the merged tree for `metadata-core`, `plugin-approvals`, `rest`, `runtime`, `mcp` and `dogfood`, each including its test-typecheck ledger.
- **Generated artifacts:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` named the references and liveness counts as stale, and both were regenerated. `check:test-typecheck` exits 0 when run on its own with more heap; inside `check:generated` it runs out of memory on this box.
- **ADR-tier review:** the ADR-0106 exception text and its anchor invariant were re-read and redrafted at the ADR tier. After that, all four ADR checks exit 0: `check:adr-anchors`, `check:adr-index`, `check:adr-symbol-anchors` and `check-adr-links`.
- **Not driven in a browser here:** whether the console request page renders Approve / Reject.
  - The card's counterfactual says it does: with masking off, the member gets meta `200` and the page renders its decision actions.
  - The page names only these two approval objects.
  - Acceptance round 2 re-runs `approvals.account-app-entry` on the frozen release sha.

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
